memory_update.text: Primary direct node candidates identified: MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, ORCL, CRWV. These have the strongest direct links to AI cloud capacity demand via capex guidance, cloud revenue, RPO/backlog, active power, or capacity constraints.

META is a major direct AI capex spender and should be included in a broader or follow-up pass, but was left out of the 5-candidate limit because its infrastructure demand is more internally monetized through ads/consumer AI than cloud-platform resale. It remains a high-priority adjacent candidate.

For this node, the strongest evidence fields to track are: AI/cloud capex guidance, cloud revenue growth, capacity constraint language, remaining performance obligations, contracted/active power, finance leases, customer prepayments, and gross margin/depreciation impact.

Second-order suppliers such as data-center REITs, power/cooling vendors, server ODMs, networking suppliers, and power utilities should be handled in separate supply-chain-node passes rather than mixed into this direct demand pass.

Key falsification trigger: if management language shifts from supply constrained to demand constrained, or if backlog/RPO conversion slows while capex and depreciation continue to rise, upstream AI infrastructure suppliers face overbuild risk.

Add CRWV as a direct public AI-cloud capacity candidate for the hyperscaler AI capex/cloud-demand node; key metrics are backlog, customer concentration, utilization, GPU financing, and backlog conversion.
Add DLR as a hyperscale/AI data-center capacity REIT candidate; use signed bookings, backlog, pre-leasing, powered-land availability, and AI-oriented leasing disclosure as primary evidence.

Add FIX as a scarce data-center construction execution candidate; evidence requires data-center revenue mix and backlog conversion, but backlog growth and prior data-center disclosure support inclusion.
Add MOD as a data-center thermal-management candidate after the May 2026 $4B long-term Airedale cooling capacity agreement; monitor customer concentration and manufacturing capacity expansion.
Add BE as an onsite power candidate tied to AI data-center grid constraints and the Oracle up-to-2.8GW agreement; monitor fuel economics, permitting, deployment cadence, and service/warranty margins.

Further Layer 1B passes should separately expand transformer/switchgear suppliers, backup generation, water/cooling materials, fiber/optical interconnect, and utility/grid owners to avoid over-concentrating this node in data-center REITs and named AI-cloud providers.
MOD is a high-priority second-order AI capex candidate for the cooling chokepoint because it has disclosed a customer-funded, multi-year, $4B data center cooling capacity agreement.

FIX maps to AI capex through mechanical/electrical and modular construction backlog rather than semiconductor exposure; key variable is whether technology/data-center backlog remains durable and high margin.

NVT should be tracked as a liquid-cooling and power/enclosure infrastructure supplier; exposure is plausible and supported by manufacturing expansion and NVIDIA-reference architecture involvement, but revenue mix requires verification.

CRDO is a connectivity chokepoint candidate for AI clusters through AECs and high-speed data-center networking; evidence is promising but needs primary-source validation for customer concentration and attach-rate durability.

APLD provides a more speculative but direct mapping to hyperscaler AI capacity through long-duration AI Factory leases; financing, construction, and power delivery risk are central falsification points.

Potential additional Layer 1B candidates not included due to five-name limit: DLR/EQIX for AI-ready data center REIT capacity, COHR/LITE/AAOI for optical transceivers, GLW for fiber/optical materials, and selected utilities/grid interconnection names.

node: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the universe for the demand node around hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand. The most direct US-listed candidates are the largest cloud platforms and AI-cloud capacity aggregators that translate enterprise/model-lab demand into data-center capex, GPU/CPU purchases, networking, power, cooling, and long-term capacity leases. This pass prioritizes direct exposure and disclosed demand signals: cloud revenue growth, explicit AI/datacenter capex guidance, remaining performance obligations, backlog, capacity constraints, contracted capacity, and active/contracted power. No investment recommendation is implied. Expanded the universe around the hyperscaler AI capex/cloud-demand node toward public companies exposed to scarce capacity, buildout execution, cooling, power, and contracted AI-cloud demand. The five highest-relevance additions for this pass are CoreWeave as a newly public AI cloud capacity provider, Digital Realty as a hyperscale/AI data-center capacity owner, Comfort Systems USA as a scarce mechanical/electrical contractor, Modine as a data-center cooling supplier with a large capacity agreement, and Bloom Energy as an onsite power supplier to AI/cloud data-center projects. These are research candidates only, not trading recommendations. Expanded universe for the hyperscaler AI capex/cloud-demand node with emphasis on second-order and potentially underappreciated public-market mappings: cooling capacity, mechanical/electrical construction backlog, liquid-cooling/power enclosures, high-speed intra-cluster connectivity, and AI-ready colocation capacity.
